sources.title: CAIIB Rules & Syllabus 2026
sources.document_date_basis: PDF creation metadata and the date in the file name; the title page says "Rules & Syllabus 2026"
sources.session_applicability: CAIIB 2026 (the page that links it lists the May/June 2026 and December 2026 examinations)
sources.note: Covers all four compulsory and all five elective papers. Syllabus on PDF pages 5-26.
established: PDF p.1: four compulsory papers and five electives; candidates choose one elective and may change it in any attempt.
PDF p.1: pass mark 50 out of 100 per subject; or at least 45 in each subject with 50% aggregate across all subjects in a single attempt.
PDF p.3: about 100 objective multiple-choice questions for 100 marks including case-based questions; the Institute may vary the number of questions.
PDF p.3: some numerical questions have no options and the answer is keyed in.
PDF p.3: online mode only; no negative marking for wrong answers.
PDF p.3: duration 2 hours.
PDF p.4: cut-off rule: exams held March to August use regulator guidelines and developments up to 31 December; exams held September to February use those up to 30 June.
PDF p.26: battery-operated portable calculator allowed, up to 8 functions and 12 digits; scientific calculators not allowed.
open_points: The illustrative cut-off table on PDF p.4 still shows 2025 sessions. The December 2026 cut-off (30 June 2026) is derived from the general rule on the same page, not from a 2026-specific table.
Six section headings are set in plain type and were inferred as headings (flagged on each topic). The extraction has not been proofread line by line by a person.

sources.title: CAIIB (Certified Associate of IIB&F) web page: examination schedule
sources.session_applicability: CAIIB 2026
sources.note: A live web page; it can change. The saved copy is the evidence for the dates below.
established: May/June 2026 session exam dates: 31 May (ABM), 7 June (BFM), 13 June (ABFM), 14 June (BRBL), 21 June 2026 (electives).
December 2026 session exam dates: 6 Dec (ABM), 12 Dec (BFM), 13 Dec (ABFM), 20 Dec (BRBL), 27 Dec 2026 (electives).

sources.title: Notice: Information and operational guidelines in respect of new set of questions 'Questions without options' from November/December 2023 CAIIB examination
sources.document_date_basis: date in the file name
sources.session_applicability: From the November/December 2023 CAIIB examination onward; no later replacement was found on the academics notice page on the retrieval date
established: Questions without options appear in all four compulsory subjects and carry one mark each.
Only digits, a leading minus sign and a decimal point can be keyed in; commas and other characters are not accepted.
Where the number of decimal places is specified, the answer is rounded to that many places (examples: 8.7678 to 8.77, 8.7623 to 8.76, 5.45678 to 5.4568).
An answer that is not saved is treated as not attempted.
open_points: The notice gives rounding examples but does not state a rule for an exact tie (a trailing 5). The app uses half-up rounding for authored answers and must avoid tie cases in questions until that is confirmed.

established: March-August 2024 exams: cut-off 31 December 2023. September 2024-February 2025 exams: cut-off 30 June 2024.

sources.title: Real Time Gross Settlement System (RTGS) FAQs
sources.document_date_basis: Date shown on the page
sources.session_applicability: Facts checked on the retrieval date; see the batch review for applicability at the 30 June 2026 cut-off.
established: RTGS: real-time, gross (no netting), settled in the books of the RBI, final and irrevocable; minimum remittance Rs 2,00,000 with no upper ceiling; available 24x7x365.

sources.title: National Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT) System FAQs
sources.document_date_basis: Date shown on the page
sources.session_applicability: Facts checked on the retrieval date; see the batch review for applicability at the 30 June 2026 cut-off.
established: NEFT: owned and operated by the RBI; batches at half-hourly intervals, 24x7x365; no RBI amount limit but a member bank may set limits with Board approval; non-account holders may remit cash up to Rs 50,000 per transaction; beneficiary credit expected within two hours of batch settlement.

sources.title: CHAPS (payments page)
sources.document_date_basis: Page carries no date
sources.session_applicability: Facts checked on the retrieval date; see the batch review for applicability at the 30 June 2026 cut-off.
established: CHAPS payments between direct participants settle individually, gross, in the Bank of England's RTGS system, and are irrevocable; the Bank of England operates CHAPS.

sources.session_applicability: Dated before the 30 June 2026 cut-off for the December 2026 session, or confirmed unchanged; see the batch review.

sources.authority: Income Tax Department, Government of India
sources.title: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 394: Collection of tax at source (table item 7, LRS remittances)
sources.document_date_basis: Income-tax Act, 2025 in force from 1 April 2026 (PIB release); page shows the Act as published for 2026
sources.session_applicability: Dated before the 30 June 2026 cut-off for the December 2026 session; see the batch review.
established: TCS on LRS remittances exceeding Rs 10 lakh: 2% for education or medical treatment, 20% for other purposes; no collection on an education loan from a financial institution; overseas tour package 2%.

sources.authority: Ministry of Finance, Government of India
sources.title: Finance Bill 2026: Explanatory Memorandum (TCS rationalisation, paragraphs on the LRS and overseas tour packages)
sources.document_date_basis: Union Budget 2026-27 presentation; the amendments were enacted as Act No. 4 of 2026 (footnotes of section 394)
sources.session_applicability: Before the 30 June 2026 cut-off; enacted with effect from 1 April 2026.
established: At present TCS at 5% on LRS remittances for education or medical treatment above ten lakh rupees; proposed reduction to 2%; overseas tour packages reduced to 2% with the threshold removed.

sources.authority: International Trade Administration, US Department of Commerce
sources.title: Know Your Incoterms (overview of Incoterms 2020)
sources.document_date_basis: Page carries no date
sources.session_applicability: Describes Incoterms 2020, in force from 1 January 2020 and still the current ICC edition (checked on the ICC page); no regulator cut-off applies to a private rule set.
sources.note: Web page, saved locally (not committed). Secondary to the ICC rules themselves, which were not retrieved.
established: Incoterms 2020: eleven rules; seven for any mode of transport (EXW, FCA, CPT, CIP, DAP, DPU, DDP) and four for sea and inland waterway (FAS, FOB, CFR, CIF); DPU replaces DAT, with the seller unloading.

sources.title: Master Direction - Export of Goods and Services, FED Master Direction No. 16/2015-16 (page shows updated as on July 17, 2026)
sources.document_date_basis: Update date shown on the page; the direction is dated 1 January 2016
sources.session_applicability: The sections used were unchanged by the 17 July 2026 update (which substituted the INR trade settlement paragraph); the nine-month realisation period was restored by FEMA 23(R)(8)/2026-RB on 5 June 2026, before the 30 June 2026 cut-off. It is superseded from 1 October 2026 by RBI directions of 16 January 2026.
established: Realisation within nine months; warehouse exports fifteen months; late documents; extension of time up to six months; reduction in invoice value; agency commission; refund; ACU settlement; advance against exports.

sources.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025, RBI/DOR/2025-26/154 of 28 November 2025 (page shows updated as on October 1, 2026), Chapter XV Export Credit

sources.session_applicability: The Directions of 28 November 2025 were in force at the 30 June 2026 cut-off. The saved page is a later version (October 2026); earlier versions were not retrieved, so a change to Chapter XV between the cut-off and October 2026 cannot be excluded.
established: Rupee packing credit (period, 360-day rule, liquidation, running account), post-shipment credit periods, advances against undrawn balances, PCFC, EBR and the Gold Card scheme.

sources.session_applicability: In force at the 30 June 2026 cut-off. It replaces the ECB framework of 2018-2019 that the courseware describes.
established: The ECB framework in Schedule I: eligible borrowers, lenders, currency, borrowing limit, maturity, cost, end-use restrictions, proceeds, security, refinancing, conversion and reporting.
